- When sentiment is strongly negative (avg < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below model output.  
- After sharp price spikes (forecast > +10% above recent high), model often overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above recent peak or use 30-day moving average as ceiling.  
- If sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates upside — add 2–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.3.  
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — adjust downward by 3–7% if sentiment < -0.2.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion — if recent 7-day average is > 10% above 30-day average, reduce forecast by 2–5% to align with mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more in 3-day window), model overfits short-term noise — smooth forecast with 5-day moving average or use sentiment-weighted average of 3–7 day window.
